applies_why: The judge text labels the Romans 1:3 issue UNDERDETERMINED on the ground that there is no explicit textual resolution of paternity, so it does the thing K-S2 governs.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: `does not state a link or its contrary`: read broadly enough to forbid using the absence of explicit textual resolution as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED, or narrowly as barring only a single omitted verse from deciding the issue while permitting a multi-verse underdetermination.
why: Because the judge's stated reason is the absence of explicit textual resolution, it falls under the broad reading and breaches K-S2.
